subject: circuits

milestone.title: Thevenin equivalents
milestone.objective: Find the Thevenin equivalent of a one-source resistor network in under 10 minutes

sources.title: Course notes p.12 (fixture)
sources.text: Any linear network seen from two terminals can be replaced by a voltage source Vth in series with a resistance Rth. Vth is the open-circuit voltage between the terminals. To find Rth for a network with only independent sources, turn the sources off: replace each voltage source with a short circuit and each current source with an open circuit, then find the resistance seen from the terminals. Example: a 12 V source with R1 = 4 kilohm in series and R2 = 12 kilohm across the terminals. Vth = 12 x 12 / (4 + 12) = 9 V. With the source shorted, R1 and R2 are in parallel: Rth = 4 x 12 / (4 + 12) = 3 kilohm.

lesson_lines: Seen from two terminals, any linear network acts like one voltage source **Vth** in series with one resistance **Rth**.
- **Vth** is the open-circuit voltage between the terminals.
- **Rth**: turn the independent sources off. Replace each voltage source with an open circuit and each current source with a short circuit, then find the resistance seen from the terminals.
12 V source, R1 = 4 kΩ in series, R2 = 12 kΩ across the terminals.
Find the Thevenin equivalent of a 9 V source with 1 kΩ in series and 2.2 kΩ across the output.

planted_errors.quote: Replace each voltage source with an open circuit and each current source with a short circuit
planted_errors.correct: Replace each voltage source with a short circuit and each current source with an open circuit
planted_errors.why: Swapped: a zero-volt source is a short, a zero-amp source is an open (source).
With the source shorted, R1 and R2 are in parallel: 4 × 12 / 16 = 3 kΩ.
